cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama House District 101 in 2026. She ran against incumbent Republican Chris Pringle. Her background, jobs and any offices held could not be confirmed from the sources available.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended by the voter guides Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust, and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, where she grew up, or when she came to Alabama. Her work history and any past offices are not documented in the sources we could read. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and her campaign site gives only a short list of priorities. Her priorities include affordable health care, better low-performing schools, higher worker pay and benefits, and pollution at Big Creek Lake, but we found no detail on her positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns or abortion. We found no news coverage of controversies or foreign ties.

cands.bio: Republican state representative for District 101 (Mobile County) and Speaker Pro Tempore of the Alabama House since January 2023. Served 1994–2002 and again since 2014. Real estate agent (Southern Timberlands), homebuilder and general contractor. Former congressional staffer. University of Alabama graduate.
cands.gaps: We found no documented actions by Pringle (bills sponsored or deeds in office) on any of the platform issues, and Ballotpedia's sponsored-legislation list did not load. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, police pay and pensions, school choice, or campaign donor pledges. His statements on abortion, guns and immigration come from his 2020 congressional campaign, not 2026. His campaign site claims credit for homestead exemption increases and teacher pay raises passed by the legislature, but we found nothing showing his own part in them. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for 2026 and no controversies appear in the pages we read. His birthplace comes from Wikipedia alone, and his upbringing from his campaign site and Ballotpedia, which quotes it.
